solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Members chasing large mammal carry weapons

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the limbs come after the animal

parts.note: a bear is a large mammal
arms are members, or limbs, of the body

explanation.surface: Limbs pursue a big beast, and somehow this means being armed.
explanation.walkthrough: The right to keep and bear arms is the phrase in mind; 'Members' as limbs misleads towards clubs or parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to carry it, and arms are weapons, so the phrase is an exact paraphrase.

clue.text: Stud manager

definitions.meaning: a stud is a raised knob or ornament on a surface
a manager is someone in charge at work, a supervisor

explanation.definitionFit: A boss is both a decorative raised stud and the person in charge of a workplace.

clue.text: Leader of America and West remains inundated

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: The head of the United States and the Western world are left swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded or covered with water, just as inundated does.

clue.text: Moan, a bollard being crushed — large vehicle carrying this?

indicators.note: being crushed means squashed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A groan as a bollard is flattened by a huge lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an oversize lorry carries one, and such a vehicle could well flatten a bollard.
explanation.definitionFit: On British roads, an outsize cargo needing escort and warning signs is officially termed this, carried by a large vehicle.

clue.text: Mother saving silver and note inside large bottle

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe within, so the parent holds the other pieces
inside confirms the metal and the note sit within the parent's word

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A mother stashes silver and cash in an oversized bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM is British for mom; 'saving' gives MAGUM and 'inside' slips N in after the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Aida's first song recalled as this?

definitions.text: Aida's first song recalled as this?

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the opera's name
recalled means called back, so the word for a tune is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: An opera fan asks whether the first number from Verdi's Aida, called to mind, was a solo.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same both ways, a nod to 'recalled'; and the whole clue describes it, since Aida is an opera full of solo songs.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo song is the kind of number Aida would open with, so the whole clue points at it.

clue.text: Official about to block charge led by soldiers

indicators.note: led by means coming after, so the soldiers go first

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

indicators.note: to block means to sit in the way, so the short word goes within the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An official is about to stop soldiers being billed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; 'led by' means the soldiers come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee is the official who enforces the rules in a match.

clue.text: A comment about City Director's first story

indicators.note: about means around, so the comment surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a note is a brief comment
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the director's title

explanation.surface: A remark about the City director's first tale.
explanation.walkthrough: EC, the postcode district, stands for the City of London, its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting story about an incident.

clue.text: Hipster actor redesigned part of theatre

indicators.note: redesigned means remade in a new form, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A trendy performer has remodelled a section of the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: This sunken area in front of the stage is where the musicians play in a theatre.

clue.text: Wrong to accept thanks for blemish

indicators.note: to accept means to take something in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A moral lapse that takes gratitude in its stride leaves a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a mark or blemish, on cloth or on a reputation.

clue.text: Mistake to capture one river animal

indicators.note: to capture means to take prisoner, so the slip surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a gaffe is a social mistake
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An error leads to seizing a single animal by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked African giraffe is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Both confused about ungroomed roan horse

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters wrap the unkempt word
confused means mixed up, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

parts.note: an ungroomed coat is rough
a roan coat is reddish, so roan gives red

explanation.surface: A puzzled pair fussing over a scruffy roan horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roan' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies letters: a roan coat has red hairs mixed with white.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred is a purebred racehorse breed, so it is an example of a horse.

clue.text: Expert taking snooker shot considered unfeasible

parts.note: crack means expert, as in a crack shot
a pot is a shot sinking a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A skilled player attempts a snooker shot thought impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot scheme is eccentric and wildly impractical, so it is deemed unworkable.

clue.text: Scoundrel runs half of La Scala? Not entirely

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: not entirely means all but the final letter of the run built from the opera house's name
half of means keep one of the two letters of the short word, here its second

explanation.surface: A villain who runs part of the Milan opera house, though not all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is Milan's famous opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, though now often used fondly.

clue.text: Half of prison allowed to have item of underwear

indicators.note: half of means keep only the first half of the prison's name

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Half the jail is permitted a vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, worn as underwear in British usage.

clue.text: A religious group will constrain person's initial view

indicators.note: will constrain means will hold within, so the group surrounds the letter

parts.note: a sect is a religious group

indicators.note: initial means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cult will keep someone's first opinion in check.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a particular view or angle on a matter, or the outlook of a building.

clue.text: Little energy in a lot of people encountering a protozoan

indicators.note: in places the energy symbol inside the crowd

parts.note: a mob is a large crowd of people
E is the abbreviation for energy, little because it is a single letter

explanation.surface: A crowd low on energy meets a tiny single-celled creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a classic protozoan.

clue.text: Millions investing in one cartel go wild for group of companies

indicators.note: investing in means putting money into, so the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
wild means out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Money pours into a cartel that then runs amok, a tale of corporate greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' belongs with the fodder, not the signal: 'wild' alone shuffles ONE CARTEL GO, and 'investing in' places M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomerate is a large corporation formed from many different businesses.

clue.text: Deliberately lose most of the argument

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the short word

parts.note: a row is a noisy argument

explanation.surface: Someone concedes the larger part of a dispute on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a match is to lose it intentionally, often for a bribe.

clue.text: Front of engine stuck in railway bank

indicators.note: stuck in means wedged inside, so the letter goes within the abbreviation
front of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A locomotive's nose has got stuck in a railway embankment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun for an embankment; it is the verb, as in bank on.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to depend on or trust them.

clue.text: Plundering is bad in a servant

indicators.note: in places the word for bad inside the servant

parts.note: a page is a young servant
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Looting is wicked, the moral of a tale about a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage is the act of plundering, especially in war; both are nouns for looting.

clue.text: Soft food: clear opening for entrepreneur

parts.note: clear means unmixed or free of contamination

indicators.note: opening for means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A business founder finds a clear opening in baby food.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is food mashed or blended to a smooth, soft pulp.

clue.text: Some into testing betting

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people get into testing their luck with a flutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is a pool-betting system at racecourses, so it stands for betting itself.

clue.text: One abandoned actors with a Method

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A performer left behind by fellow actors who follow the Method school.
explanation.walkthrough: Method acting is a famous technique, which makes 'Method' look like theatre jargon rather than a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A castaway is someone shipwrecked or marooned, left alone somewhere remote.
